description: The provided image is a multi-layered, concentric pie chart (often called a sunburst or radial tree chart) that visually represents the hierarchical categorization of language content from the paper “A Multi-Task Benchmark for Abusive Language Detection in Low-Resource Settings.” The chart is divided into two primary outer segments: “Abusive” (in teal) and “Not Abusive” (in yellow), each occupying roughly half of the chart, suggesting a balanced dataset or classification outcome. Within the “Abusive” category, subcategories include “Political,” “Racial,” “Sexist,” “Religious,” and “Other,” each further subdivided by sentiment: “Negative,” “Mixed,” and in some cases “Positive” or “Neutral.” For example, “Political” and “Other” under “Abusive” are predominantly “Negative,” while “Religious” includes smaller segments for “Positive,” “Mixed,” and “Neutral.” The “Not Abusive” category similarly branches into “Political,” “Religious,” “Other,” and “Neutral,” with sentiment labels such as “Positive,” “Negative,” “Mixed,” and “Neutral” distributed across them. The chart uses color coding and segment size to indicate relative proportions, with larger segments representing higher frequencies. The innermost circle contains a small gray bar, possibly indicating an overall metric or placeholder. This visualization effectively illustrates the multi-task nature of the benchmark by showing how abusive and non-abusive content are further classified by topic and sentiment, highlighting the complexity and granularity of the dataset.
